questions.q: Why is On-Demand the most expensive EC2 pricing model per hour?
options: It carries no commitment, so AWS prices in the ability to stop paying at any time
It is only available for the largest instance types
It requires a 3-year upfront commitment
It is reserved exclusively for Spot workloads
questions.explain: On-Demand trades a higher hourly rate for zero commitment — pay only for what's running, stop paying the instant it's no longer needed.

questions.q: What does a Reserved Instance (RI) commit you to?
options: Using only Spot capacity for a full year
A specific instance family in a specific Region for a 1- or 3-year term, in exchange for a discount
A specific amount of S3 storage
A one-time payment with no ongoing commitment
questions.explain: An RI ties the discount to a specific instance family and Region for a 1- or 3-year commitment.

questions.q: How does a Savings Plan differ from a Reserved Instance?
options: It can only be purchased for a 6-month term
It offers no discount at all compared to On-Demand
It applies only to Spot Instances
It commits to a dollar-per-hour spend instead of a specific instance family, applying the discount more flexibly
questions.explain: A Savings Plan commits to spend (dollars/hour) rather than a specific instance family, letting the discount apply across instance families, sizes, and Regions for Compute Savings Plans.

questions.q: What is the main tradeoff of using a Spot Instance?
options: It costs more than On-Demand but never gets interrupted
It can only run in a single, fixed Availability Zone
AWS can reclaim it with a two-minute warning when it needs the capacity back
It requires a 3-year commitment like a Reserved Instance
questions.explain: Spot Instances offer a steep discount off On-Demand in exchange for the risk of a short-notice reclaim by AWS.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, which pricing model fits the nightly batch job best, and why?
options: Spot Instances, because the job can simply restart if interrupted and the discount is worth that small risk
Savings Plans, because the job's usage pattern is identical to a production database
On-Demand only, because batch jobs can never tolerate interruption
Reserved Instances, because batch jobs always run continuously
questions.explain: A job that can checkpoint or simply restart tolerates Spot's reclaim risk well, making the steep discount a good trade.
